page.layout: One printed page of text in a single column, with marginal notes on the right. Running head at top, page number at top right. Footnote marks 1, 2 and 3 stand in the right margin beside the text. Catchword at lower right, gathering signature at lower left. The strip at the left edge is the neighbouring page and is not transcribed.

main_text.p: tis præmia decernuntur, vel legum violatoribus constituta sunt supplicia, vel indiscriminatim utriflibet in judiciis jura dicuntur? quorum sunt illi, Legum actus primi, & per modum Formæ: isti remotiores, & per modum Effectus. Annon eo demum fine, ut Respublica in pace & tranquillitate floreat; & ut privati etiam cives publicæ felicitatis participipio, pro suo cujusque modulo & mensura, gaudeant & fruantur? hoc est uno verbo, ut communi utilitati inserviatur. Probatur denique tertio, 3. à Posteriori, ex omnium hominum sensu consensuque. Nam & qui Prov. 8. 15.justa decernunt Legumlatores, revera videntur; & qui Psal. 94. 10.meditantur malum sicut Legem, videri tamen cupiunt, in ferendis legibus non tàm suam, quàm communem utilitatem respexisse. Εἴτε σαφρονῶν[?], εἴτε ἀληθείας[?], five id sincerè intendant, five subdole obtendant, qui Leges aliis dicunt; propositum fuisse sibi in ferendis Legibus Bonum Publicum, profitentur utcunque universi.

II. Hoc ita jacto disputationis fundamento, Legum finem esse Bonum Communitatis; ad Dubia pergo. Quorum esto primum, an sit Legum Humanarum usus aliquis, saltem necessarius? Cui nullus foret in hac (Dubiorum dico) classe concedendus locus, nisi hoc nobis facesseret negotium Anabaptistarum, aliorumque cum ipsis juxta sententiam, vesanus error. Ex quorum principiis, (quum negent licere viro Christiano Magistratum gerere, bello liteve contendere, jurare aut alteri juramentum deferre aliaque consimilia :) consequi videtur, omninò nullam esse Legum Humanarum necessitatem. Nec enim erit, sublatâ Jurisdictione, qui Leges ferat: nec sublatis Judiciis, qui reformidet.Horat. 3. Ode 24. Quid testes quærimonia, si non supplicio culpa reciditur? Quid vana sine moribus

page.notes: Left edge strip is the neighbouring page, not transcribed. The Greek phrase after "meditantur malum sicut Legem" is hard to read and is uncertain throughout. The first footnote reads "Prov. ?." with a number that is unclear; read as 8 with 15 below it. Footnote 2 "Psal. 94." and "10." are both read from the right margin. The note "Horat. 3." is in the right margin, with "Ode 24." on the line below. The right margin number "3." beside "tertio" is a section numeral, given as a note. Printed letter forms such as "liteve" and "vana sine" are uncertain; "Quid vana sine moribus" continues past the end of the scan. Long s is printed as f throughout and is transcribed as plain s.
